Herbert Jeffrey Hancock (born April 12, 1940) is a jazz  pianist and composer from Chicago, Illinois, United States. Hancock is one of jazz music's most important and influential pianists and composers. He embraced elements of rock, funk, and soul while adopting freer stylistic elements from jazz.

As part of Miles Davis' "second great quintet" Hancock helped redefine the role of a jazz rhythm section, and was later one of the first jazz musicians to embrace synthesizers and Jazz funk.

title: Get Up With It
desc_lfm_album: Get Up With It is a double album by American jazz trumpeter Miles Davis, released in 1974 on Columbia Records. It is a dense and sprawling work primarily composed of recordings from 1970 to 1974, showcasing Davis's evolving electric jazz fusion sound and his deepening exploration of funk, rock, and avant-garde elements. The album is notable for its extended track lengths, its incorporation of diverse musical textures, and its status as a bridge between the more explicitly rock-influenced *On the Corner* and the introspective *Agharta* and *Pangaea*. title: On the Corner
desc_lfm_album: Miles Davis' On the Corner, released on October 11, 1972, is one of the most polarizing and innovative albums in the history of jazz and beyond. It marked a significant departure from traditional jazz forms, embracing a fusion of funk, rock, avant-garde, and electronic influences. Davis created On the Corner with the intention of appealing to a younger African-American audience that had shifted its attention from jazz to funk and rock. title: Kamakiriad
desc_lfm_album: Kamakiriad is the second solo album by Steely Dan singer Donald Fagen, released in May 25, 1993 by Release. It was his first collaboration since 1980 with Steely Dan partner Walter Becker, who produced the album. The album is a futuristic, optimistic eight-song cycle about the journey of the narrator in his high-tech car, the Kamakiri (Japanese for praying mantis). It was nominated for a Grammy Award for Album of the Year in 1993. The album follows a lengthy writer's block for Fagen; the songs are based on personal observations about middle age (as 1982's The Nightfly is lyrically described .
desc_lfm_artist:

Fagen is known for his use of complex jazz harmonies, elaborate arrangements, and exacting attention to detail and launched his successful, if sporadic solo career in 1982.

desc_lfm_album: Memory Serves is a 1981 album by the New York based No Wave music group Material. .
desc_lfm_artist:
Material is a musical group formed in 1979 and led by bass guitarist Bill Laswell.

In 1978, having received a substantial royalty payment for his work with The Yardbirds, Georgian music entrepreneur Giorgio Gomelsky relocated to New York  in an attempt to open up the American market to the European progressive rock/jazz-rock bands he was working with, such as Gong, Henry Cow and Magma. He established the Zu Club in Manhattan and after meeting 24 year old bass player Bill Laswell, encouraged him to form a band.
